sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a cycle, not a straight line.

Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 [D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72], then climbed 23.9% in FY2021 [D231] and 16.5% in FY2023 [D322] before falling 15.6% in FY2024 [D367] and 11.7% in FY2025 [D412].
The FY2024 decline came as rising global grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates cut large and small agriculture shipment volumes [P17].
In FY2025 Production & Precision Agriculture sales volumes fell 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil [P10].
Production Agriculture was the largest driver, at 37.1% of FY2025 revenue [D657], and its 17.6% decline subtracted 7.0pp from revenue growth [D658][D659].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue [D889], fell 11.8% and subtracted 3.0pp [D890][D891], while Financial Services at 13.8% of revenue [D922] fell 3.1% and subtracted 0.4pp [D923][D924].
Operating costs fell 7.3% in FY2025 [D425] while revenue fell 11.7% [D412], so operating costs fell 4.4pp less than revenue [D431].
Net income fell 29.2% in FY2025 [D413] against a 27.8% fall in diluted EPS [D415], as the diluted share count dropped 1.9% [D427].
The FY2025 contraction was broad, with the two equipment segments accounting for most of the decline and only Financial Services holding near flat.
Operating margin was 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], above the 12.1% window median [D1335] but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1334].
In FY2024 the 3.7pp margin decline [D378] came with SG&A costing 1.9pp [D391] and R&D 0.9pp [D390], as SG&A rose 5.3% [D381] on revenue down 15.6% [D367].
In FY2025 net margin of 11.0% [F50] sat 2.7pp below FY2024's 13.7% [F49][D422], while the effective tax rate was 20.1% [D400].
The FY2025 net margin of 11.0% [F50] remains above the 9.6% window median [D1338], but the direction is now two years of compression.
Operating cash flow of $7.46 billion [F80] was 1.48x net income in FY2025 [D401], above the 1.17x window median [D1364].
The FY2025 inflow was driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in receivables related to sales [P5].
Free cash flow of $6.10 billion [F100] was a 13.4% margin [D398], above the 11.6% window median [D1341], with capex at 3.0% of revenue [D397] and 0.61x D&A [D403].
Cash conversion has held up through the downturn, which cushions the earnings decline.
Cash and equivalents were $8.28 billion at FY2025 [F140], up 13.0% [D420], against $13.8 billion of current debt [X185].
Long-term debt was last reported at $32.9 billion in FY2021 [F146], and the pack omits total debt and net cash after that break [R9].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.86 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D409][D410], down from $8.64 billion in FY2023 [D319].
Return on average equity fell to 20.6% in FY2025 [D411], below the 28.3% peer median [D1362].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025, by 15.6% and 11.7% [D367][D412][R1].
Two consecutive double-digit declines mark a genuine downcycle in the core agriculture business, not a one-year air pocket [R1].
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [D657][D658][R2].
The largest segment is also the weakest, so a recovery in the top line depends on large agriculture shipments turning [R2].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so total debt and net cash after that omit it [R9].
The leverage picture cannot be read from this pack for the latest four years, which limits any balance-sheet conclusion [R9].
Whether FY2026 revenue growth turns positive from the FY2025 base of $45.7 billion [F10], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether operating margin recovers toward the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1334] from the FY2024 level of 17.5% [F30], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether free cash flow margin holds above the 11.6% window median [D1341] from the FY2025 level of 13.4% [D398], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
